name: Revenue recognition — use by others of enterprise resources yielding interest, royalties and dividends
definition: Revenue from letting others use the enterprise's resources is recognised only when no significant uncertainty as to measurability or collectability exists, and then on a basis fixed per kind: interest on a time proportion basis using the amount outstanding and the rate applicable; royalties on an accrual basis in accordance with the terms of the relevant agreement; dividends when the owner's right to receive payment is established.
why_it_exists: These three are not earned by delivering anything, so neither a delivery date nor a measure of performance is available. AS-9 replaces the missing trigger with a different one for each: elapsed time for interest, contract terms for royalties, and the establishment of a legal right for dividends. Collapsing them into one rule would recognise dividends before they are declared.
inputs: which kind of yield it is: interest, royalty or dividend
for interest: amount outstanding, rate applicable, period elapsed
for royalties: the terms of the relevant agreement, and the substance of the transactions
for dividends: evidence that the right to receive payment is established
whether the payer is in a foreign country requiring exchange permission
outputs: revenue recognised for the period on the basis fixed for that kind
preconditions: the revenue arises from the use by others of enterprise resources, not from a sale of goods or a rendering of services
no significant uncertainty as to measurability or collectability exists
exceptions: royalties may be recognised on some other systematic and rational basis where, having regard to the substance of the transactions, that is more appropriate than the agreement terms
where interest, royalties or dividends from foreign countries require exchange permission and uncertainty in remittance is anticipated, recognition may need to be postponed
common_mistakes: accruing dividend income for a period before the right to receive payment is established
recognising interest on receipt rather than on a time proportion basis
applying the royalty agreement's stated schedule mechanically where the substance of the transactions points to a different systematic and rational basis
recognising foreign interest, royalties or dividends in full while remittance permission is uncertain
treating the discount or premium on debt securities as a gain on maturity rather than as accruing over the period to maturity
legal_references: UNKNOWN — statutory backing not extracted from any downloaded source in this pass
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — GST treatment of interest, royalties and dividends is a separate determination and must not be conflated with accounting revenue recognition
evidence_required: for interest: the loan or security document showing the amount outstanding and the rate applicable
for dividends: the document establishing the right to receive payment
for foreign sources: evidence of exchange permission or of anticipated uncertainty in remittance
confidence_factors: weak when the rate applicable or the amount outstanding is absent from the document
weak when the royalty agreement is not available and only a remittance advice is
weak when a dividend is evidenced only by a credit in a bank statement, which does not by itself show when the right was established
weak when the source is foreign and the document is silent on remittance
validation_checks: no significant uncertainty as to measurability or collectability exists, or recognition is postponed
interest recognised equals amount outstanding × rate applicable × the time proportion elapsed
no dividend is recognised earlier than the establishment of the right to receive payment
the royalty basis used is the agreement's, or a stated systematic and rational alternative justified by the substance of the transactions
examples: a loan of a stated principal at a stated rate, three months elapsed — recognise three months of interest on a time proportion basis
a licence agreement fixing royalty per unit sold, licensee's sales statement received — accrue in accordance with the agreement's terms
counterexamples: an expected dividend on a shareholding where no right to receive payment has yet been established — not recognised
an appreciation in the value of a shareholding — an unrealised holding gain, outside the definition of revenue (AS 9 para 3), not a dividend
